text: DSH Dev Workflow 是面向 DSH Web 的开发工作流插件。它在工具执行前检查提交、PR 和发布约定，并提供提交信息与文档同步工具。功能包括 Conventional Commits 校验、PR 描述检查、版本与 changelog 核对，以及 /dev-workflow 手动命令；设置面板可调整规则。适合希望 agent 遵循仓库规范的开发者。需要 Node.js 20 以上和 DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 或 0.2.1-rc.2。

DSH Dev Workflow checks commit, PR, and release conventions in DSH Web. It validates messages, documentation changes, PR sections, versions, and changelogs. A /dev-workflow command and settings panel support manual checks and configuration. Requires Node.js 20+ and DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 or 0.2.1-rc.2.

DSH Dev Workflow 的功能「提交信息检查」：DSH Dev Workflow 的功能「提交信息检查」：校验提交标题是否符合配置的类型、scope 和格式规则，并给出错误或提示。提交动作前可自动触发，也可通过工具执行。
DSH Dev Workflow 的功能「文档同步检查」：DSH Dev Workflow 的功能「文档同步检查」：根据变更文件检查成对文档是否一起更新，并提示代码变更缺少文档或 changelog 更新。可由检查工具或手动命令触发。

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · dsh-dev-workflow：

A conventions gate for DeepSeek Harness (dsh)

check the commit message before it commits · the PR description before it opens · the version before it releases · ask before a command that cannot be undone · 200–250 tokens resident

dsh plugin --profile web add @melosic/dsh-dev-workflow

---

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · dsh-dev-workflow：If your `git commit`, `gh pr create` and `git tag` are run by an agent, these checks are for you. The rest of this file covers only when it speaks up, and why.

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Why：Every project writes some conventions down — how a commit message is shaped, which sections a PR carries, how a version is chosen. They usually live in `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and a document or two.

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Why：Text does not enforce itself. Reading a rule and following it are two different things: the guide says the subject stays under 50 characters and the agent still writes 62. This plugin turns the parts a machine can check into checks that run — at commit, pull request and release time — and stops to ask before anything irreversible.

What it saves is rework:

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · When it speaks：| You are | It does |
| --- | --- |
| `git commit` | Checks the message format, whether a `feat` added a CHANGELOG entry, and whether docs moved with the code |
| `gh pr create` | Checks the description for the sections the template asks for, unticked checklist items, and a linked issue |
| `git tag` / `npm publish` | Checks the version is semver, that tag and `package.json` agree, and that the changelog has the section |
| `git reset --hard`, `rm -rf`, `git push --force` | Stops and asks first |
| Reading `.env`, a real secret in the arguments | Refuses — no per-call approval |

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · When it speaks：The rest of the time it says nothing.

What it says when it stops you is one line of why, plus the safer alternative:

> **A force push rewrites remote history and can discard other people's commits.**
> Prefer `--force-with-lease`: it refuses to overwrite commits you have not seen.

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · How it works：The plugin hangs off DSH's tool-execution chain. Before the agent runs a command or writes a file, it looks once:

One layer judges "is this within the rules" — commit messages, PR descriptions, version numbers. The other judges "can this be undone" — lost work, rewritten history, things others will see. When both fire, there is one prompt showing both sets of reasons, never two questions in a row.

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · How it works：The full spec is not on this path either: it stays resident as one summary line and is read only when needed, which is why the resident cost is 200–250 tokens.

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · The five guards：| Guard | Blocks | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command | `rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, `dd of=/dev/sda` — irreversible | ask |
| git | `reset --hard`, `clean -f`, `push --force`, branch deletion, `--no-verify`, `git restore .` | ask |
| Outward | `push`, `tag`, `gh pr create`, `npm publish` — others will see it | ask |
| Sensitive files | `.env`, `*.pem`, private keys, `credentials` | deny |
| Credentials | A real secret in the command arguments | deny |

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · The five guards：The first three ask rather than refuse: most of these actions are legitimate, they are just worth one confirmation. The last two refuse — reading a private key has no "fine once you confirm it" case, and printing the path in an approval dialog is itself a second leak, so there is no per-call approval. The false positives are already excluded: sample files such as `.env.example` do not count, and neither does `grep -rn "credentials" .` — the check that tells you whether a secret is in the tree, because a search expression is not a path. To make one file readable, drop it from `fileGuard.noRead` or turn that guard off.
@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · The five guards：In a session with approvals turned off, "ask" becomes a refusal, and the prompt says how to get past it.
@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · From the window：This is the only path that needs no terminal, and it works in the desktop app too.

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Command line：Install it into the profile you boot dsh with. If you start with `dsh web`, that is `web`:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @melosic/dsh-dev-workflow
```

The templates that ship with dsh are `web`, `headless`, `acp`, `sdk` and `sdk-minimal`; a profile of your own takes its own name.

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Command line：**The desktop app is the exception**: its profile is `desktop`, and the plain `dsh` command refuses to manage it (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`). Use the CLI the app ships:

```bash
"<desktop install>/resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add @melosic/dsh-dev-workflow
```

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Command line：Use DSH's installer rather than `npm install`: a profile only loads the bundles named in its own `dsh.profile.bundles` list, and the installer is what writes both the dependency and that entry.

```bash

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · update / uninstall — copy the profile prefix from above：dsh plugin --profile web add @melosic/dsh-dev-workflow@latest
dsh plugin --profile web remove @melosic/dsh-dev-workflow
```

Reload dsh, then run `/dev-workflow status` to confirm it is working:

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · update / uninstall — copy the profile prefix from above：If the first line says "is on", the install worked. If it says "off for this session" or "this one is NOT marked", the plugin is deliberately doing nothing — type `/dev-workflow on`, or create the marker file described in the next section.

text: @melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Configuration：The defaults are the common ones (Conventional Commits, Keep a Changelog). Everything a machine can check is adjustable — the type list, whether a scope is required, subject length, which PR sections are expected, the changelog category names, which publishing tools count. Tuned to your guide, it is that project's gate rather than this repository's. The full field list is in [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](docs/CONFIGURATION.md).

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Boundaries：- It does not replace CI. It is a pre-flight check; CI is the verdict.
- It does not review code, run tests, or format anything.
- It does not decide for you: the question is asked of you, and your refusal stands.
- It does not guess. When it cannot read the commit message or the changed-file list, it says that rule did not run instead of reporting a pass.
- Some paths it cannot see are listed under "what we cannot see" in [docs/TRIGGERS.md](docs/TRIGGERS.md). That table is a promise, not a disclaimer.

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Requirements：| Component | Version | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Harness runtime | `0.2.0-rc.2` or `0.2.1-rc.2` | `dsh --version` |
| Node.js | `>=20` | required by dsh itself |
| pnpm | any; not checked | only needed by `dsh plugin`, and it must be on `PATH` |

@melosic/dsh-dev-workflow README · Requirements：Those are the only two versions, not a range: they are the ones this plugin has actually been loaded on, and a range would also claim every 0.2 prerelease in between and every 0.3 after them. The cost is that a new DSH prerelease needs a new release of this plugin — which is the honest direction, because "not tested" should read as "unsupported". When the version is one of the others, **`dsh plugin add` refuses the install outright** (`dsh: installation rejected: Plugin … is incompatible with dsh …`, nothing is installed) and prints the `dsh plugin allow-version` escape hatch. An already-installed older copy behaves differently: the plugin is disabled at startup with `dsh: disabling profile plugin …` on stderr, and the rest of the profile loads normally. Both say why; neither is silent. Check `dsh --version` against the list above before filing a bug, and paste the output of `/dev-workflow status` into the issue; how the list is chosen is in [docs/PUBLISHING.md](docs/PUBLISHING.md).
